newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Berisha report sends EU to dinner.
newsitem.headline: Berisha report sends EU to dinner.

text.p: A report that Albania's President Sali Berisha had resigned -- later denied from Tirana -- prompted European Union foreign ministers to halt their discussion of the crisis and go to dinner instead.
Ministers from the 15-nation bloc were planning to work late into the evening to forge a difficult joint position on Albania.
One diplomat said they were about to tell their spouses -- who accompany them on such jaunts -- to enjoy the evening in the Dutch countryside without them.
Then Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said a Greek television station was reporting that Albania's chief Sali Berisha had stepped down.
All discussion ended. Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told reporters the ministers had put off their work because without Berisha everything in Albania would be different.
"If the stumbling block is no longer there, there is a fair chance of this violence being dissipated," he said.
The only problem was that the "stumbling block" was apparently not going anywhere.
A statement from his office in Tirana said that Berisha had no intention of resigning his post.
The confusion, however, had already done its work. The ministers were off to dinner, pledging to return to the subject of Albania on Sunday.
